review_type: independent labeled row-9 semantic and native-face acceptance
decision: The rounded face design and the up/right portion of row 9 pass. 112.5 has real subtle rightward yaw with downward pitch. At 135 and 157.5 the intended right component is not reliably visible at native size: the faces read mainly as centered down. Repair those two down-right heads before advancing the row.
method: Judged the actual labeled native row, source head crops, and cardinal reference. A nearest-neighbor enlargement of the last three actual source head crops was used only to confirm facial geometry. Large yaw and true profile were not required; the criterion was a visible physical right bias while retaining the rounded two-eye character.

row_findings.landmarks: Frontal face, eyes and nose presented upward, compact rounded lower face and short chin.
The cheek/nose turn and reduced far-eye presentation introduce a visible right component while the eyes and face remain upward.
Both eyes remain visible with the viewer-right eye more foreshortened; the tiny nose and cheek contour turn right without lengthening the chin.
Similar to 45 but still visibly turned right and pitched upward. Similarity does not create a wrong-quadrant defect.
Moderate physical right yaw, a fuller near eye/cheek, narrower far-eye/cheek presentation, and a short rounded chin. Both eyes remain visible and the right direction is readable.

The face is pitched down but still has a visible rightward cheek/nose turn. The viewer-right far eye is visibly narrower than the near eye and closer to the far facial edge. This is a real mild three-quarter right head, not merely a frontal down face.

row_findings.semantics: reads mainly down; right component not reliable
row_findings.landmarks: Downward pitch is clear, but the small nose and rounded chin read centered beneath the fringe and eyes at native size. The two-eye/cheek presentation is too close to a frontal bowed face to supply a reliable physical right turn. Minor asymmetry in the enlarged crop does not give a stable rightward direction in the native cell.

row_findings.semantics: reads mainly down; right component not reliable
row_findings.landmarks: The face is nearly frontal and bowed, with both eyes presented at similar prominence and a centered short chin. Neither the tiny nose/cheek contour nor the eye presentation provides a reliable rightward bias at native size. The pose cannot be confidently separated from centered down by its facial direction.

face_quality.evidence: All eight faces retain the rounded cheek, tiny nose, short chin, and large violet two-eye character. No return to the old long flat jaw, protruding chin, or one-eye full-profile style is visible.

head_scale_identity_and_registration.evidence: Head scale and rendering remain coherent across the row, and the full native figures retain a consistent body placement and ground baseline. No conspicuous scale or attachment defect was found.

blockers.evidence: The down direction is readable but the physical right component is not reliably visible. These two cells therefore do not yet establish the intended down-right quadrant at native size.
blockers.smallest_source_repair: In the complete row source, revise only the 135 and 157.5 heads to retain a mild rightward nose/chin/cheek turn under the existing down pitch. Use the accepted 112.5 head as the structural reference: subtly compress the far viewer-right eye/cheek and expose the fuller near cheek, while keeping both eyes visible, the tiny nose, round cheek, and short chin. Do not restore full profiles or a long jaw. Preserve the accepted first six heads, body artwork, and registration.

uncertainty: This is row-9 source/native proof acceptance only. Final despill, exact atlas assembly, row-10 transitions, and complete animation acceptance remain for a later review.
